notes: One canonical question per ask, shared by Skill 49 (launch and legacy), Skill 71, Skill 83. Same questions and same answers file in claude-nine, Claude Code and OpenClaw; only the rendering differs. choices has at most 3 entries; the renderer always adds the help_label option. never_default questions are never defaulted; every other question may fall back to its default, flagged 'to confirm'. Launch-automation questions (spec 3.5) apply to launch and bf modes, never legacy; the launch date and the sender facts are never defaulted, so no deadline or sender is invented. Mode page is Skill 71's page-only profile (profiles.page): one page, not a funnel, and it opens the client's existing answers file so every confirmed launch answer is reused instead of asked again. The profile's question list is the ask list for a page run. A signature page always needs its canonical renders, so the image questions no longer offer a no-pictures option. The payment-plan flag is derived from billing and is never asked; see system_fields.payment_plans.
introduction: Let's build a launch that fits your business. I'll help you clarify what you're selling, who it helps, and how to present it. Then we'll turn your approved plan into the supported launch pages and follow-up materials. We'll take one question at a time. You can ask for an example, ask me to recommend an answer, or ask me to use what you've already shared. You'll review the plan before we build.
question_estimate_template: about {n} short questions, depending on what we already know

actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.
coaching.actions_rule: Every question comes with a short reason and these three ways to get help. When the client is unsure or stuck, open coaching: 'I don't know' and its equivalents are help requests, never a substantive answer the flow then skips past.
coaching.when_unsure: Reflect back what you understand from what they have shared, offer two or three concrete options with the reason for each, and ask one simple follow-up question. Never merely repeat the question. Never say you cannot guess. Offer a draft answer they can confirm; a genuinely unknown fact stays unknown.
coaching.examples_rule: An example must fit this client's own situation and use only the context this client has authorized - never another client's information. Mark clearly what is a known fact they gave you, what is your reading of it, and what is only a suggestion. Never invent prices, testimonials, results, inventory, promises or credentials.
coaching.recommendations_rule: A recommendation is a proposal for the client to review. It is never a silent decision and never approval for spending. Paid work needs its own separate OK, and the three assistance preferences can be changed later at any time.
coaching.language_rule: Speak like a patient, capable business partner. Use everyday words and translate marketing terms as you go. Schemas, IDs, hashes, provider routing and similar technical details stay invisible to the client. Never present yourself as a licensed therapist and never turn the conversation into a psychological diagnosis.
coaching.one_at_a_time: One question per turn. Reuse what the client already confirmed instead of asking again, and never repeat confirmed answers after a pause and resume. Prefer a relevant follow-up over mechanically advancing the list. Progress updates at stage milestones and near completion count only the questions that actually apply, and a changed estimate is explained.
coaching.offers_rule: Develop one offer at a time: who it helps, the result they want, what can realistically be delivered, what is included, and price guidance. Summarize that offer back before considering another one, and ask whether another package would genuinely help. Recommend the simplest setup that fits; never automatically add upsells, downsells or extra products.
coaching.black_friday_rule: For a seasonal promotion, the same coaching plus the seasonal decisions asked one at a time: promotion dates; the offer, discount or bonus; real limitations; existing customers versus new buyers; delivery and follow-up. Never invent urgency or scarcity. Explain how a discount, bonus or bundle could fit their circumstances, then confirm their choice. The image and style questions are a small part of the interview, never the whole of it.

sections: What we understand and recommend, and why
What will be built and what it is meant to do for your business
Assumptions, limitations and any costs still to confirm
plan_review.rule: Use the existing plan review - no extra approval gates. The client can change any item or approve that exact plan. Approval is never a reason to ignore their answers, and nothing in the review promises guaranteed sales.

page.description: The page-only interview for one BlackCEO Signature page, and the page run's exact ask list: ask these questions and nothing else. It asks the offer, audience, proof, story, brand, image and length questions a page needs (including the one offer-shape question that decides price versus packages), and never the funnel length, page set, bump, upsell or downsell extras, account setup, launch-automation or plan-approval work that belongs to Skill 49. Record the page kind (sales or opt_in) before length: an opt-in landing page is long-form only and the engine refuses standard for it. Every page needs its canonical renders, so there is no no-images answer.
page.reuse: Confirmed answers are never re-asked: a page run opens the client's existing answers file with --mode page, every launch answer already confirmed is reused, and only the open questions of this profile are asked - the shared bank's full queue is never walked on a page run. A never_default answer stays open; it is never inferred from the earlier run.

questions.text: What is the best way for me to help you with your launch?
questions.why: It sets how much I suggest and how much I ask - and you can change it later.
choices: A: Recommend a plan for me (use what is known, ask only what is missing, let them review)
B: Guide me through each decision (explain options, help them choose)
C: I already have a plan (help act, flag anything important missed)

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: You can change this preference at any time. Anything I recommend is only a proposal for you to review - never a silent decision, and never approval to spend money.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

default.value: B: Guide me through each decision (explain options, help them choose)
default.reason: Most people want a guide through the decisions; you can change this any time.

choice_explanations.A: Recommend a plan for me (use what is: I use what you have already told me, ask only for what is missing, and put the plan in front of you to review before anything is built.
choice_explanations.B: Guide me through each decision (expla: I explain each decision in plain language, walk the options with you, and help you choose.
choice_explanations.C: I already have a plan (help act, flag: You bring the plan; I help you act on it and flag anything important it misses.

questions.text: What is the business outcome you want from this launch? One sentence is plenty.
questions.why: Every page and message serves this outcome, and it keeps the plan honest about what a launch can realistically do.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think about what would make this launch worth it - more sales of one offer, filled seats, a first group of paying clients. A rough answer is fine.
examples: Fill all 12 seats in my group program before the end of November.
Get 30 new sign-ups for my workshop.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: What is making that hard right now?
questions.why: The page and the follow-up answer your real obstacle instead of a guess.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say what is in the way in your own words. If there is more than one obstacle, name the biggest one first.
examples: People visit my page but never book a call.
My list is small and I do not know how to reach new people.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: What is your business or brand name, exactly as it should appear on your pages?
questions.why: It goes on the page and the checkout, and becomes your logo text if you have no logo file.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Type it the way you want customers to see it, with your capital letters.

questions.text: What is the exact name of your offer, as it should be written on the page?
questions.why: The name is used word for word. I never invent or change it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This is the title of what you sell: a course, event, program or service.

questions.text: In a sentence or two, what are you offering, and who is it for? A rough sentence, a link or pasted notes are all fine.
questions.why: The offer and its buyer anchor every later choice, and the claims on the page come only from what you say here.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say what it is and who it helps. You can paste your own notes.
examples: A 6-week group program that helps new coaches get their first 10 paying clients.

questions.text: Who is this for? Name at least one kind of person and what they want. More than one is welcome when they want different things.
questions.why: The page speaks to these people directly.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think of the people who buy from you today. What result do they want, not the steps to get it?
examples: New coaches who want their first paying clients
Busy moms who want to start a side business

questions.text: What will be different for someone after they use it?
questions.why: It is the realistic result the page promises. I will never invent a guarantee.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Finish this sentence: after this, my buyer can ___ within ___.
examples: After 6 weeks you have a clear offer and 3 conversations booked.

questions.text: What are the three biggest problems it solves for them? Short phrases are fine.
questions.why: The page is built around three distinct problems.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: One about their day-to-day, one about how they privately feel, one about who sees them stuck.
examples: Family asking when they will get a real job

questions.text: What does the buyer actually get? A rough list is fine. Include amounts, access time or dates where you know them.
questions.why: What buyers get is a promise they rely on, so it must be yours.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: List every item: modules, calls, templates, bonuses.

questions.text: Do you have real results, stories or kind words from buyers that we may use? Paste or link them, or say none yet.
questions.why: Proof must be real and credited. If you have none yet, the page is written without it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A testimonial, a result with a number, or a screenshot you have permission to share.
examples: "I booked 3 clients in 2 weeks." - Dana R.

default.reason: No proof is invented; the page is written without a proof section.

choice_explanations.I have some to share: Real words from real buyers are the strongest proof. Paste or link whatever you have.
choice_explanations.Use my own story: Your own experience can carry the page instead of buyer quotes.
choice_explanations.None yet: That is completely fine. The page is built without testimonials - nothing is invented.

questions.text: Share any founder context you want the page to use: how you got here, who you built this for, and what you want them to know about you. Skip anything private. This one is optional: leaving it blank is a complete answer.
questions.why: The personal letter on the page can carry your real context, and only the parts you choose to share.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Professional background, credentials, or the reason you started all count. Nothing sensitive is required. A blank answer leaves the letter written from what you already told me.

questions.text: How do you talk? Give me 2 or 3 words, or paste a paragraph you wrote that sounds like you.
questions.why: The copy is written in your voice.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Words like warm, direct, funny, calm, bold.

default.reason: A neutral friendly voice until you give your own.

questions.text: Who should appear in the images, and how should the people break down? Give percentages, or say no people at all.
questions.why: I never assume who appears in your images.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say who your buyers are and who you want shown. It can be anyone, including no people.

questions.text: Will buyers choose one offer, a few packages, or levels that build on each other?
questions.why: It decides whether you need a page where buyers choose, and how many pages the funnel has.
choices: Levels that build on each other

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: One offer: everyone buys the same thing. A few packages: buyers pick one (like Basic or Premium). Levels: each higher level includes the one below it.
examples: Levels: Level 1, 2 and 3, each adding more

choice_explanations.One offer: Everyone buys the same thing - the simplest, clearest funnel.
choice_explanations.A few packages: Buyers pick between clearly different options.
choice_explanations.Levels that build on each other: Each level includes the one below it.

questions.text: Let's do the packages one at a time, in your own words. For the first one: who is it for, what result does it give, what is included, and what does it cost?
questions.why: A page where buyers choose is built only from the packages you describe and price. I never invent one, and no special format is needed.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Plain sentences are fine. We finish one package, I summarize it back, and then we decide together whether another one would genuinely help.
examples: Premium: twelve lessons, four live calls and templates, $497.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: Do you already have a price for it, or should I suggest a starting price for you to review?
questions.why: A price is a promise to your buyer. I only use a price you gave or a suggestion you approved.
choices: Suggest one for me to review

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think about what the result is worth to the buyer, and what similar programs charge. I can suggest a range with my reasoning, but you approve it.

choice_explanations.I have a price: Your price is a fact we can build on.
choice_explanations.Suggest one for me to review: I suggest a starting price with my reasoning; it stays a proposal until you approve it.
choice_explanations.It is free: A free offer still needs a clear page and follow-up.

questions.text: How do buyers pay: all at once, monthly, or in parts?
questions.why: The payment plan changes what the checkout shows.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: All at once is one payment. Monthly repeats. In parts splits one price into a few payments.

default.reason: The simplest checkout until you choose.

choice_explanations.In parts or trial first: Several smaller payments, or a low-cost trial first.

questions.text: How big do you want this funnel: 3-step, 5-step or 7-step?
questions.why: It sets how many extra offers you build.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: 3-step: page, one upsell, thank-you. 5-step adds a smaller-yes offer and a second upsell. 7-step is the full set: checkout, two upsells, two smaller-yes offers, thank-you.

choice_explanations.3-step: The essentials: main page, checkout, thank-you.
choice_explanations.5-step: Adds one extra offer after the purchase, with its own page.
choice_explanations.7-step: Adds the full chain of extra offer pages.

questions.text: Would a small extra item help them use what they are buying? It appears as an optional add-on before they pay.
questions.why: It is optional on the checkout and starts unchecked.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A small, low-priced extra, like a checklist or a bonus session.

default.reason: No add-on is built until you name one.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You already have a small add-on in mind.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: I suggest one only if it genuinely helps them use what they bought.
choice_explanations.No add-on: A clean checkout with nothing extra is a good choice.

questions.text: After they buy, is there a useful upgrade or extra product you want to offer?
questions.why: Upsell 1 adds value on top of the purchase.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Something that helps them get the result faster or go further.

default.reason: No upsell is built until you name one.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You have a next step ready for people who want more.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: Only from what you have told me, and only if you can deliver it.
choice_explanations.No upgrade: Keeping the funnel to the main offer is often the simplest, strongest choice.

questions.text: If they pass on that upgrade, is there a smaller version or an easier way to buy it?
questions.why: A smaller yes keeps a buyer who is not ready for the big one.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A lighter version or split payments.

default.reason: No downsell is built until you name one.

choice_explanations.Yes, a smaller version: A lighter version of the upgrade for people who pass.
choice_explanations.Yes, easier payments: The same upgrade on friendlier payment terms.
choice_explanations.No downsell: Their no is accepted - no second pitch.

questions.text: After someone takes the upgrade or the smaller offer, should we offer one more helpful product?
questions.why: Upsell 2 is one more optional step.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A bigger or faster option, like done-for-you or a VIP day.

default.reason: No second upsell is built until you name one.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You have one more genuinely different product to offer.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: Only if your facts include a distinct third product - never a repeat.
choice_explanations.No second upsell: One extra offer is often plenty.

questions.text: If they pass on the second upsell, what is the smallest true yes you can offer?
questions.why: A last smaller offer keeps buyers who are not ready.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A starter tier, one seat, or recordings only.

default.reason: No second downsell is built until you name one.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You have the smallest true yes ready.
choice_explanations.Easier payments: The same offer on smaller payments.
choice_explanations.No second downsell: After this the funnel simply thanks them.

questions.text: Which pages should I build?
questions.why: Every page you build gets desktop and phone sketches and designs.
choices: Only the main page and checkout

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: The pages are: opt-in page, sales page, page where buyers choose, checkout, upsell, smaller-offer page, and thank-you. The recommended set builds all the ones your funnel uses.
examples: Recommended: landing, sales, checkout, upsells, thank-you

default.reason: The full recommended set for your funnel shape.

choice_explanations.Every page my funnel needs (recommended): The full journey is built so no buyer hits a dead end.
choice_explanations.Only the main page and checkout: The minimum to take a payment; extras can come later.
choice_explanations.Help me choose: I recommend the smallest set of pages that serves your plan.

questions.text: What are your brand colors? Send color codes like #1A2B3C, or color names. If you have a logo or a website, I can read the colors from it.
questions.why: Every sketch and design is made only in your own colors.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Brand colors are the 2 to 4 colors on your logo, website or business cards. A color code is the # followed by six letters and numbers.

default.reason: A neutral palette that belongs to no client, used until you send your own.

questions.text: Which of these is your MAIN color: the one people think of first when they think of your brand? {colors}
questions.why: The main color is used for buttons and key headlines.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: If you are unsure, pick the color that is most on your logo, or the one you use for buttons on your website.

default.reason: Your first color is used as main until you pick.

questions.text: Which color is your SECOND color, the one that supports the main color? {colors}
questions.why: It is used for section backgrounds and supporting shapes.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: The second color is usually softer or darker than the main color.

default.reason: Your next color is used until you pick.

questions.text: Which color should be the small highlight color for badges and underlines? {colors}
questions.why: An accent adds a little spark. The other colors stay as extras.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Pick the brightest of what is left, or choose none.

default.reason: The next color is used as the highlight until you pick.

questions.text: What should the page background be?
questions.why: Text has to be easy to read on it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Light backgrounds feel open and clean. Dark backgrounds feel premium and dramatic. Most coaching pages use light.

default.reason: Light is the easiest to read.

choice_explanations.Light (white or cream): Clean and bright - the easiest to read.
choice_explanations.Dark: A darker canvas for a bold, premium feel.
choice_explanations.Not sure: I pick a background that gives your text the best contrast.

questions.text: Do you have a logo file we can use?
questions.why: Your real logo is used as is. I never redraw it.
choices: Use my business name as text

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A logo file is a PNG or SVG of your logo. If you have none, your business name is set in clean type as a text logo.

default.reason: Your business name is shown as a text logo until you send a file.

choice_explanations.I will send it: Your real logo is reused exactly as it is.
choice_explanations.Use my business name as text: Your business name set as clean text stands in.
choice_explanations.Not sure: Send whatever you have and I will sort it out.

questions.text: Do you have brand fonts, the typefaces on your logo or website?
questions.why: Fonts give the page its personality.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A font is the shape of the letters. If you do not know, I pick a pair that suits your brand and show you.
examples: Playfair Display for headlines, Source Sans 3 for text

default.reason: Fonts are chosen to suit your brand and shown to you to confirm.

choice_explanations.I know my fonts: Your existing typefaces keep the brand familiar.
choice_explanations.Pick good ones for me: I choose a readable pairing that suits your brand.
choice_explanations.Not sure: Point me at your website or logo and I will read them from there.

questions.text: Do you want a real photo of you on the page? If yes, send one or two clear photos.
questions.why: Real people build trust. I never generate a lookalike of you.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A clear, well-lit photo of your face works best. If you send none, the page has an empty photo frame you can fill later.

default.reason: An empty photo frame is used; no likeness is generated.

choice_explanations.Yes, I will send photos: A real photo of you builds trust.
choice_explanations.No photos of me: The pages are built to work beautifully without one.
choice_explanations.Not sure: You can decide later - nothing is invented.

questions.text: Do you give us permission to use the photos you send on your page and ads for this launch?
questions.why: I only use photos of people with their permission.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This covers photos of you and anyone in them. You can withdraw it any time.

default.reason: Without a clear yes, your photos are not used.

choice_explanations.Yes, I give permission: Your photos may appear on the pages and follow-up.
choice_explanations.No: Understood - they stay off the pages.
choice_explanations.Not sure: Nothing is used until you say yes.

questions.text: Which look do you want for your page: A, B or C?
questions.why: The style sets the shape of the photos and sections.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A Block: clean rectangles, classic and polished. B Circle: round photos with colored rings, warm and friendly. C Hybrid: Block structure with round photos only for personal pictures. If you are unsure, tell me three words for how you want your brand to feel.

default.reason: Block is the most neutral look.

choice_explanations.A Block: Rectangles and clean edges - structured and confident.
choice_explanations.C Hybrid: A mix of both - balanced and flexible.

questions.text: Optional: do you have a registered design style card id (it starts with FN-)? Leave blank if not.
questions.why: It locks every image to that style.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Only if you were given one. Most people skip this.

questions.text: Which image service should make your pictures?
questions.why: I only name a service after checking it works for you. Every page needs its generated pictures; there is no no-images option.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This is the service that draws the generated photography each page section is built around. If you are not sure, I use the one already connected to your account. Logos and photos you send are placed as files and never generated, and paid pictures still need your separate OK.

default.reason: The standard connected image service.

choice_explanations.My connected service: The image service already connected to your account.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: I recommend one only after checking what is actually available.

questions.text: What is the most pictures I should make for this launch?
questions.why: It is a ceiling, not a purchase. Paid pictures also need your separate OK.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Every image stage renders one image per copy section, per platform, so each page needs its full canonical set and cannot be built with none. 12 covers a single page, 24 a small funnel, 36 a full one. These are generated photography costs; logos and photos you send are placed as files for free, and paid pictures still need your separate OK.

default.reason: A modest ceiling; raising it needs your OK.

choice_explanations.12: A tight set - one page's canonical sections.
choice_explanations.24: A fuller set across a small funnel.
choice_explanations.36: A full set across a large funnel.

questions.text: Do you approve spending on paid pictures, and what is the most you want to spend?

choices: Yes, up to a limit I will give

help.explain: Nothing paid is made until you say yes with an amount. Sketches and free drafts do not cost anything.

questions.text: Should the main page be the standard length, or the long, detailed version? An opt-in landing page is long-form only; standard is for a sales page.

default.reason: Optional; you can add it later.

choice_explanations.No, not this launch: Replies are handled by you as usual.
choice_explanations.Yes, add the bot: A bot answers common replies while you stay in control.

questions.text: After someone pays, do they need a log-in or an access link from you?
questions.why: It decides whether the access email, the access automation and the delivery link are planned.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Choose yes for a course, membership, or event that needs a log-in, a link, or a schedule. Choose no for a service where a person follows up by hand.

choice_explanations.Yes, send access after purchase: Buyers receive their log-in or access link automatically.
choice_explanations.No, nothing to deliver: Nothing digital to hand over after payment.

questions.text: Where should buyers land after they pay — the access page or log-in link?
questions.why: The full launch plan refuses without a usable access destination; it is where the access email and the welcome message send people.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Paste the address buyers reach after payment, for example a member log-in page or a download page on your own site.

questions.text: Will this offer be paid in full, or do you offer payment plans?
questions.why: Payment plans turn on the failed-payment recovery automation; without them it is never built. The flag comes from the billing answer, so this is only read, never asked.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Choose payment plans if a buyer can split the price into installments. Your billing answer still decides how the checkout charges them.

questions.text: What sender name should people see on your emails and texts?
questions.why: It is the name in the From line and the text signature; it must be real and recognizable.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Use the name your audience already knows: your business name or your own name. Never use a name you do not own.

questions.text: Which email address should replies go to?
questions.why: Real replies must reach a mailbox you read.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Any address you check, like hello@yourdomain.com. It has to be a real mailbox, not a no-reply address.

questions.text: Are you approved to send text messages to your list? (Phone carriers require a business texting registration; if you are not sure, I will help you find out.)
questions.why: Texts cannot send until this approval is in place; without it every text stays a draft.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This is the registration phone carriers require before a business can text its list. If you do not know, that is fine - say the word and I will help you find out.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

default.reason: Texts stay drafts until you confirm A2P approval.

choice_explanations.No, not yet: Texts stay drafts until the approval lands.

questions.text: I need three real facts: your community link, what the bonus is, and a yes that you will really send the personal text.
questions.why: The pages only promise what you will do.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Give the real community URL, name the bonus, and confirm you will send the text.
examples: https://example.com/community; Bonus: planner PDF; text confirmed: yes

questions.text: Is this launch kit included in what you bought or have a license for?
questions.why: A launch is only built with a confirmed right to run it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: I check this against your account record. I never assume it.

choice_explanations.Yes, it is included: Covered by what you already have.
choice_explanations.Please check for me: I verify it against your account record before anything runs.
choice_explanations.No: This launch needs its own arrangement.

questions.text: What is the heart of this promotion: a discount, a bonus on top, or a special bundle?
questions.why: Each can work in different circumstances; the plan confirms your choice before anything is built.

choice_explanations.A discount: Lowers the price for the promotion window - right when buyers are ready and your numbers allow it.
choice_explanations.A bonus: Adds extra value at the same price - right when a price cut would cost too much.
choice_explanations.A special bundle: Combines things they usually buy separately - right when you have pieces that naturally go together.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Tell me which fits your circumstances and why, or say what you have in mind in your own words. Nothing is invented and no pressure is added to the page.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: What are the real limits on this promotion? For example how many you can serve, what is ready to deliver, or any date you cannot move.
questions.why: Only real limits go on the page. Urgency or scarcity is never invented.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: If there are no special limits, say so - that is a real answer. Only limits that are true of your business are used.
examples: I can only take 20 new members at this price.
The bonus is ready now, but the main program starts in January.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: Is this promotion for people who already bought from you, for new buyers, or both?
questions.why: Who the promotion is for shapes the offer wording and the follow-up messages.
choices: People who already bought from me

choice_explanations.People who already bought from me: A thank-you offer for loyal customers; the follow-up speaks to them as past buyers.
choice_explanations.New buyers: A welcome offer for first-time buyers; the follow-up introduces you properly.
choice_explanations.Both: Both groups can buy; each follow-up speaks to where they already are.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: There is no wrong answer - it simply decides how the page and the follow-up speak to people.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: After someone buys in this promotion, what should happen next for them? Rough notes are fine.
questions.why: Buyers should know exactly what happens after they pay; your delivery answers are reused instead of asked again.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think thank-you note, delivery details, anything they should watch for. We build on the delivery answers you already gave.
examples: A thank-you email today and the access link straight away.
A short note about when their bonus arrives.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.text: Here is the plan I recommend. Do you approve it for building, or would you like a change?
questions.why: Approval is tied to the exact plan you saw.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Nothing is built until you approve.
